findings.title: Sharded queries are interpolated N+1 times: once in runShardSplitQuery and again in every runSplitQuery sub-request
findings.body: runShardSplitQuery (shardQuerySplitting.ts:49-52) now maps every target through datasource.applyTemplateVariables before grouping by stream shard, and then executes each shard group by building a subRequest and calling runSplitQuery. With this change, runSplitQuery also maps every target through datasource.applyTemplateVariables (the new .map here), so in the shard-splitting flow each query is interpolated once up front plus once per shard-group sub-request. The updated test 'Interpolates queries before running' in shardQuerySplitting.test.ts now expects applyTemplateVariables to have been called 5 times for a single target (1 upfront + 4 shard batches), which bakes this redundancy into the test suite. Variable substitution ($var, $__auto, step) is effectively idempotent so this mostly wastes work, but request.filters is passed on both calls, so ad hoc filters are appended to the stream selector twice unless applyTemplateVariables dedupes them — producing duplicated label matchers in the LogQL selector sent to Loki. Consider interpolating in only one place (e.g. let runSplitQuery skip interpolation when the caller already interpolated, or have the shard path rely on a single interpolation point).

findings.title: No test coverage for ad hoc filters (request.filters) through the split/shard query paths
findings.body: This change newly threads request.filters into datasource.applyTemplateVariables in runShardSplitQuery (previously it called interpolateVariablesInQueries with only scopedVars, so ad hoc filters were never applied to sharded queries) and in runSplitQuery (which previously did not interpolate targets at all). None of the added or updated tests set request.filters and assert the resulting selector — they only cover replacement of variables in expr and step. Because the shard path now invokes applyTemplateVariables multiple times per target (the updated 'Interpolates queries before running' test expects 5 calls for one query), a duplication or loss of ad hoc matchers in the final LogQL selector would go unnoticed. A test passing request.filters through both splitting paths and asserting the final expr would close the gap.
